domain: Political Economy / Social Policy / Labor Economics
topic_summary: Analysis of Universal Basic Income as a contested kernel where the same policy instrument (unconditional cash transfer) is read through fundamentally different normative frameworks. The freedom-floor reading treats UBI as expanding individual autonomy and reducing coercive labor relations. The dependency-trap reading treats UBI as state-induced atrophy of work ethic and market participation. Each reading emits constraints with inverted victim/beneficiary structures.

key_entities: Universal Basic Income (unconditional cash transfer policy)
Labor market (site of wage negotiation and employment relations)
Welfare state apparatus (existing means-tested transfer system)
Precarious workers (gig economy, part-time, contingent labor)
key_tensions: Individual autonomy vs work obligation (freedom to refuse exploitative work vs duty to labor)
Unconditional transfers vs means-testing (dignity vs targeting efficiency)
State capacity vs market discipline (redistribution authority vs employment constraint)
mechanisms: Exit threat enhancement (workers can refuse low-wage jobs, shifting bargaining power)
Labor supply reduction (fewer workers seeking employment at given wage)
Skill atrophy feedback (prolonged non-employment reduces employability)
absences: Capital taxation incidence (who ultimately bears the tax cost of UBI funding)
Care work valuation (UBI's effect on unpaid domestic/community labor)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The income-support commitment: that a society should provide material subsistence independently of market participation
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Competing normative frameworks (liberal autonomy theory, work-ethic conservatism, republican non-domination, paternalist welfare theory) each claiming authority to interpret what income support legitimately is

readings.commitment: Income support expands negative liberty by removing coercive market necessity
readings.expected_structural_delta: Precarious workers enter beneficiary set; employers of low-wage labor enter victim set (reduced labor supply raises wages or reduces profitability)

readings.commitment: Income support atrophies self-sufficiency and market discipline
readings.expected_structural_delta: Future recipients enter victim set (skill atrophy, reduced employability); current taxpayers enter beneficiary set (if UBI prevents and is cheaper than means-tested welfare expansion)

readings.commitment: Income support recognizes and values non-market productive labor
readings.authority_grounding: Feminist economics / care work valuation frameworks
readings.expected_structural_delta: Unpaid caregivers enter beneficiary set; market-wage earners subsidizing non-market work enter ambiguous position (benefit from care provision, bear tax cost)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Freedom-floor holds that autonomy-from-necessity is the foundational good; dependency-trap holds that obligation-to-labor is the foundational good. No single framework can simultaneously treat exit-from-labor as both liberation and harm.

axes.human_readable: Freedom-Floor Reading: UBI as Exit-Threat Enhancement
axes.structural_delta: Unconditional income removes coercive necessity from labor market participation, expanding workers' exit options and shifting bargaining power
axes.primary_observable: Wage floor movement in low-skill sectors post-UBI implementation; quit rates in exploitative employment
axes.selection_reason: Primary reading of kernel; distinct beneficiary/victim structure from sibling readings

axes.human_readable: Dependency-Trap Reading: UBI as Skill-Atrophy Mechanism
axes.structural_delta: Unconditional income reduces labor market participation, inducing skill atrophy and long-term employability decline
axes.primary_observable: Employment rates among UBI recipients over 3-5 year window; skill-matched wage trajectories for non-participants vs participants
axes.selection_reason: Axiom-contradictory reading; inverts victim structure from freedom-floor reading

axes.human_readable: Care-Economy Reading: UBI as Non-Market Labor Subsidy
axes.structural_delta: Unconditional income legitimizes and funds unpaid care work, shifting productive activity from market to household/community
axes.primary_observable: Time-use surveys (hours in unpaid care work); gender wage gap movements; child/elder care quality metrics
axes.selection_reason: Structurally independent reading surfacing absence (care work); different observable and beneficiary set

axes.structural_delta: The distribution of tax burden for UBI funding determines who ultimately bears cost
axes.primary_observable: Tax incidence analysis (statutory vs economic burden); capital flight metrics; effective corporate tax rates
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: upstream mountain but all three selected readings implicitly handle funding questions; lower structural distinctiveness than readings themselves

axes.structural_delta: Technological unemployment increases political demand for UBI as compensatory mechanism
axes.primary_observable: Labor force participation rate; automation penetration by sector; unemployment duration trends
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: upstream context but not a reading of the income-support kernel itself; captured in freedom-floor's exit-threat mechanism

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Tax burden distribution for UBI funding
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Upstream mountain feeding all three readings; lower priority than readings themselves which embed funding assumptions

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Technological unemployment as UBI demand driver
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Upstream context captured within freedom-floor's exit-threat mechanism; not a reading of the kernel

omegas.description: If long-term UBI pilots show neither significant exit-threat effects NOR skill atrophy, both primary readings collapse. The kernel may not be contestable on structural grounds—only on predicted magnitudes of agreed mechanisms.

Does UBI trigger price inflation that nullifies purchasing power gains? If full passthrough occurs, freedom-floor constraint reclassifies as scaffold (nominal transfer with no real effect). Dependency-trap reading survives if labor-supply reduction is real.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + F03 risk on freedom-floor's epsilon estimate

omegas.description: Care-economy reading depends on reliably measuring unpaid labor value and quality. If time-use surveys are insufficient observables, the reading's epsilon bin may shift or independence from freedom-floor may collapse.
omegas.source: Primary observable adequacy check for care_economy_reading

omegas.description: Freedom-floor and dependency-trap hold axiom-contradictory foundations yet both are socially live positions. This is licensed plurality: no arbiter exists to settle the normative dispute, so both readings persist as constraints on policy space.
omegas.source: Axiom contradiction declaration + edge type analysis (coexists_with + contradictory axioms)

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: All three readings assign mod epsilon bins but empirical evidence from existing pilots (Kenya GiveDirectly, Stockton CA, Finland) shows mixed and context-dependent magnitudes. Generated omega_empirical_collapse and omega_inflation_passthrough to bound this uncertainty. Care-economy reading's epsilon depends on measurement infrastructure (omega_care_work_measurement).
